background_notes.fact: At the fixed positive t0, g(x)=u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0) is smooth and ∂_{x_j}g=∂_{x_j}u_t·∂_{x_j}u+u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u.

grounds.reason: All component derivatives of u exist and are smooth on the open domain.
u_t is the componentwise time derivative.
Spatial derivatives use the stated coordinate convention.

background_notes.justification: Express the Euclidean dot product as a finite sum of component products and differentiate term by term with the scalar product rule. Partial derivatives of a smooth function are smooth.

background_notes.fact: For compact C contained in (−R,R)^n with R>0, C is disjoint from a neighborhood of ∂[−R,R]^n. A function zero outside C is therefore zero at both endpoints of every coordinate-j segment through this box.

grounds.reason: N002 supplies compact C, R>0 and C⊂(−R,R)^n.
At t0∈int J, N002 makes the positive-order derivatives and hence g zero outside C.

background_notes.justification: If C is nonempty, each coordinate absolute value attains its maximum on C, and the maximum over finitely many coordinates is strictly less than R. The resulting positive margin separates C from the boundary. If C is empty the assertion holds everywhere. A coordinate segment endpoint has coordinate j equal to ±R and lies on that boundary.

background_notes.fact: For n≥1 and a valid coordinate j, T transports the product of Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R]^(n−1) and Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R] to Lebesgue measure restricted to Q=[−R,R]^n. The zero-dimensional factor for n=1 has mass one. Integrals transform accordingly.

grounds.reason: n≥1, so n−1 is a nonnegative dimension.
The boxes and the bijective coordinate insertion T are explicitly constructed.

background_notes.justification: The coordinate map is a continuous linear bijection with continuous inverse. On rectangles, both the transported product measure and Euclidean Lebesgue measure assign the product of the same side lengths. Uniqueness of finite measures on the Borel sets of the box gives equality there; completion preserves this equality for Lebesgue measurable sets. The corresponding integral equality follows first for indicators, then simple functions and integrable functions. With no remaining coordinates the empty product of side lengths is one, giving the singleton factor.

background_notes.fact: Hfun is integrable on the compact product box, and for every y in Qrest its slice z↦Hfun(y,z) is interval integrable on [−R,R]. The restricted measures in S002 are finite and hence s-finite. Also, the derivative of z↦g(T(y,z)) is Hfun(y,z).

grounds.reason: Hfun is a continuous coordinate pullback of a derivative of g; the boxes have finite side lengths and R>0.
The dimensions are finite, including the specified zero-dimensional case.

background_notes.justification: Continuity on each compact box gives a finite absolute bound and measurability. The measures have finite masses (2R)^(n−1) and 2R, so a bound K gives finite integral of the absolute value, at most K times the relevant finite mass. This proves both product and slice integrability. A finite measure itself provides an s-finite decomposition. Since T(y,z) varies only coordinate j at unit speed, differentiating the restriction of smooth g to this coordinate line gives ∂_{x_j}g(T(y,z))=Hfun(y,z).

background_notes.fact: For −R≤R and an integrable real function on this interval, its oriented interval integral equals its Lebesgue integral restricted to [−R,R].

grounds.reason: R>0 and interval integrability hold for each slice.

background_notes.justification: For ordered endpoints the interval integral uses the interval between them; changing inclusion of endpoints alters only two singleton sets of one-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero.

background_notes.fact: If integrable real functions h,a,b on ℝ^n satisfy h=a+b and all vanish outside Q, then their integrals over ℝ^n equal their integrals over Q and ∫h=∫a+∫b.

grounds.reason: F001 proves the pointwise product identity, absolute integrability and vanishing outside C⊂Q.
F004 gives the zero integral of h=∂_{x_j}g over Q.

background_notes.justification: Each function equals its product with the indicator of Q, which is exactly restriction of its integral to Q. Linearity of the Lebesgue integral for integrable summands follows by decomposition into positive and negative parts, all with finite integrals. Thus the displayed product identity can be integrated without any convergence exchange.

background_notes.fact: The function y↦∫_[−R,R] Hfun(y,z) dz has integral zero against Lebesgue measure restricted to Qrest.

grounds.reason: F003 proves that this function is zero at every y∈Qrest.

background_notes.justification: The restricted measure assigns zero mass to the complement of Qrest. The function therefore equals zero almost everywhere for that measure, is integrable there and has integral zero.
